title: Unbounded pro-etale direct image commutes with open restriction
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and $p:V\to T$ a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $i:W\hookrightarrow T$ be an arbitrary open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and set $U=V\times_TW$, with projections $k:U\hookrightarrow V$ and $r:U\to W$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and the uncompleted unbounded derived operations [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. For every $L\in D(V_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ the canonical restriction map
$$\rho_L:i^*Rp_*L\longrightarrow Rr_*k^*L$$
is an isomorphism, natural in $L$. Its normalization is the termwise equality $i^*p_*I=r_*k^*I$ on a K-injective representative $I$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex]; on $Q\to W$ both sides evaluate on $V\times_TQ=U\times_WQ$, with the same restrictions and $A$-actions. Open restriction $k^*$ preserves K-injectives, using $k_!\dashv k^*$ [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-adjunction] and exact $k_!$ [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact]. With exact extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero] and its open unit [lem-exc-proetale-open-unit], this gives the natural isomorphism
$$\lambda_M:i^*Rp_*k_!M\xrightarrow{\rho}Rr_*k^*k_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rr_*M$$
for every $M\in D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$. No properness, cohomological-dimension bound, boundedness or etale-origin hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Put k = pullback.fst p i and r = pullback.snd p i. Base change makes k an open immersion [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]. The specified proEtaleOpenRestrictionComparison is definitionally the hom of sfProperOpenDerivedRestriction A r k i p (IsPullback.of_hasPullback p i).flip. That existing isomorphism derives the sectionwise fibre-product restriction identification, using the exact open adjunction and preservation of K-injectives. Its hom is invertible as a natural transformation, and therefore so is every component. Its construction already supplies naturality and the prescribed sectionwise normalization; no new resolution or independence proof is required here.

source.place: Tags 08BJ and 070Y; the existing sfProperOpenDerivedRestriction construction in lean/Sheaf/AlgebraicGeometry/ProperExceptionalOpenBaseChange.lean implements the termwise comparison and composition isomorphisms.

proof.text: For every intrinsic module sheaf M, [lem-exc-proetale-open-unit] makes the unit of [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-adjunction] at M invertible. Componentwise invertibility gives an invertible unit natural transformation. The fully faithful left-adjoint criterion makes the common extension-by-zero functor fully faithful. Apply the same criterion to sfIntrinsicOpenAdjunction, whose right adjoint is the intrinsic module pullback of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], to make its unit invertible as well. This passes between the two presentations of open restriction without asserting equality of their adjunctions.

Both extension by zero and intrinsic pullback are exact, by [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact] and [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Their termwise derived functors are the functors of [prop-exc-open-adjoint]. Compose the inverse derived-composition isomorphism, the derived image of the inverse open unit from step 2, and the derived identity isomorphism. This gives an isomorphism from the composite derived extension and pullback to the identity. The adjunction criterion Adjunction.isIso_unit_of_iso then makes the unit of the actual specified exceptionalOpenAdjunction invertible. Finally unfold proEtaleOpenRestrictionLambdaInverse: it is whiskerRight of this unit followed by whiskerLeft of the inverse restriction isomorphism of step 1. Functors preserve isomorphisms, so whiskering and composition make this specified natural transformation invertible. All functors are on the entire unbounded derived categories; no new boundedness or properness hypothesis is introduced.

source.place: Tag 09BN; exact termwise localization and Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Monad.Adjunction, Adjunction.isIso_unit_of_iso. The existing mapDerivedCategoryCompIso, mapDerivedCategoryNatIso and mapDerivedCategoryIdIso implement the canonical derived comparisons.
